_doc: The edges dataset: one-shot evaluations at the ends of each library's domain, where the money dies. Each probe is one call of one op with arguments given as expressions (mpf literals, e, pi); gen_edges.py encodes them into every representation (scripts/ladder/edge-inputs.json), test/ladder/Edges.t.sol runs them through EdgeRunner, edges.py computes the truth and writes docs/benchmarks/edges.{json,md}. Argument kinds: x, y are values in the representation; n is a plain integer passed unscaled.

ops.label: ln(x)
ops.why: The logarithm near one is where a per-second rate lives: ln(1 + r) for r = 1e-9 has eight digits on an 18-decimal grid.

ops.label: exp(x)
ops.why: exp below -42 is zero on an 18-decimal grid and has one digit at -40: every probability, discount or decay smaller than 1e-18 is gone.

ops.label: sqrt(x)
ops.why: The root of a tiny number: sqrt(1e-20) is 1e-10, which the grid holds, but 1e-20 itself is zero on it.

ops.label: pow(x, y)
ops.why: A base near one to a large power: per-second rates over years, and Uniswap's tick range 1.0001^(+-887272).

ops.label: mul(a, b)
ops.why: Tiny times tiny: a fee on a fee, a unit price times a unit size, below 1e-18 is zero.

ops.label: div(a, b)
ops.why: Small over large, and one over tiny.

ops.label: W0(x)
ops.why: The principal Lambert branch near its branch point -1/e, where the slope is infinite; only Solady has it among the others.

ops.label: W-1(x)
ops.why: The secondary branch, toward zero from below; BL127 only.

ops.label: log1p(x)
ops.why: ln(1 + x) as an op: the libraries without it compute ln(1 + x), and 1 + x is where x loses its digits.

ops.label: expm1(x)
ops.why: e^x - 1 as an op: the libraries without it compute exp(x) - 1 and the one cancels the digits.

ops.label: compound(r, n)
ops.why: (1 + r)^n for an integer n: per-second rates over years. BL127 and Maker take an exact integer power; the rest exp(n ln(1 + r)).

ops.label: powu(x, n)
ops.why: An integer power. Solady's rpow, PRBMath's powu, ABDK's pow and Maker's rpow square at the format's precision; BL127 on a 256-bit mantissa.

ops.label: erf(x)
ops.why: The error function; the libraries without it run the same series and continued fraction through their own ops.

ops.label: erfc(x)
ops.why: The tail of the normal distribution: erfc(6) is 2e-17, erfc(9.3) one ULP of BL127, zero on an 18-decimal grid from about 6.4.

ops.label: normCdf(x)
ops.why: N(d) of Black-Scholes: zero on an 18-decimal grid from d = -8.3, two ULPs of BL127 at -13.

the input is zero on an 18-decimal grid
Uniswap's top tick, 3.4e38: one bit past BL127's word
Uniswap's bottom tick, 2.9e-39: one ULP of BL127
